correctness.rationale: For odd x, the 2-adic analytic interpolation F(x)=sigma*(sigma*x)^x is well-defined on the two mod-4 branches. The binomial-series identity F(x+h)-F(x)=sigma*h modulo 4h proves isometry, well-defined finite permutations, and strong slopes. Exact first displacements are 2*v2(x-1) on the +1 branch and 1+v2(x+1) on the -1 branch. The product identity x F(x)=(-x)^(x+1) and composition formula F^2(x)/x=(-x)^(x F(x)-1) establish v2(F^2(x)-x)=3*v2(x+1), with all factors in 1+4Z_2. An elementary doubling lemma then proves all power-of-two iterate valuations; minima give the exact least periods. Counting the 2^(k-r-1) members of each valuation shell gives the full cycle census. The attached independent graph enumeration agrees at k=1..16 and 1,016 sampled iterate valuations; this is supporting finite evidence, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object study, Holden–Richardson–Robinson, arXiv:1609.06696, proves binary fixed-point counts (Corollary 11) and two-step rooted closed-walk counts (Corollary 19); its Section 6 discusses longer walks as future work. These counts do not determine the period of arbitrary odd classes. The present branchwise valuation laws and explicit entire cycle census at every level strictly extend the published low-period statements without claiming those statements new. Holden–Robinson (2012), Section 6 treats inverse fibers at odd primes, a noncovering object/parameter regime. Searches of aliases, periodic return counts, unit permutations, and published mathematical-result records revealed no source implying the all-period census. Remaining historical-priority risk and abstract-only access to a 2010 related article are recorded.

value.rationale: The finite functional graph of a natural nonlinear arithmetic map on 2^k units has exponentially many states but is completely classified by two simple valuation parameters for all k. The nontrivial difference between linear displacement near -1 and quadratic displacement near +1, the cubic two-step contact near -1, and the exact doubling of return valuations explain genuinely structural phenomena. The resulting full period spectrum, precise multiplicities, and exactly two maximal cycles at every k>=6 go beyond an isolated arithmetic computation or known low-period count. This classification is useful for arithmetic dynamics of congruence maps and interpretation of purported pseudorandom self-power iteration.
